segments.title: Chương 313: 0315 [Cả nhóm cùng phục kích Trần Quý Lương]
segments.content:
Chen Guiliang strolled all the way to the summit forum venue.

When he passed by the Sohu booth, he found that not only was Zhu Hong being surrounded, but the "Cat Girl Sextet" was also causing a sensation.

Six beautiful women were dressed in hot pants and tube tops, wearing cat ears on their heads and dragging cat tails behind them. Four of them were even wearing leopard print.

Even Chen Guiliang couldn't help but steal a few glances at the stage, only to discover that one of the cat girls looked a lot like Ariel Lin. She had the face of a good girl but was dressed in a wild leopard print outfit. The sense of contrast was absolutely amazing.

There was another cat girl who not only had a great figure but could also strike all sorts of seductive poses. Her expressions and movements were extremely provocative. Her name was Gu Zhen, a student at the Shanghai Theatre Academy.

Many of the beautiful women at Sohu's booth today were selected directly from the Shanghai Theatre Academy.

Charles Zhang really knows how to have fun!

"Quick, get a picture of him! Get a picture of him! That guy is back again!"

A commotion broke out.

The one causing the commotion was an unremarkable-looking man.

He had already earned the nickname "Hug Man." He would wander around the various booths and ask for a hug whenever he saw a beautiful woman. Many of the showgirls found it hard to refuse, so he ended up hugging a beauty every few minutes on average.

This made all the old lechers, who were secretly titillating but outwardly reserved, green with envy.

"Damn, I really want to beat him to death."

"That son of a bitch is actually going to ask Ah Zhu for a hug? Damn, Ah Zhu agreed!"

This "Hug Man" was, in fact, also creating hype, trying to become an internet celebrity in an unconventional way.

And he could enjoy the perks along the way.

Chen Guiliang walked past the Sohu booth and soon arrived near the Shanda booth.

Shanda's showgirls went for sheer numbers. Dozens of girls in revealing outfits stood in a straight line, completely still. Their overall looks were only so-so, but arranged in formation, they were particularly spectacular. It was unclear which clever little imp had come up with the idea.

The planner must frequent "one-stop" brothels.

To attract attention, the major vendors were truly pulling out all the stops.

*Audition Online* had invited VCGirl, the C-pop string trio under Emperor Entertainment Group. *Kicks Online* invited Huang Jianxiang of "not a one-man show" fame.

*Super Dancer Online*, with gameplay similar to *Audition Online*, went even further, inviting Korean star Bae Seul-ki, as well as Qi Wei, who had risen to fame in the last two years. They also brought in the main cast of the TV series of the same name.

Shanda's *Dead or Alive Online* was the most playful. It was an online game based on *Dead or Alive*. They had set up a separate sub-booth, complete with a swimming pool and beach chairs, and even trucked in several tons of sand to spread on-site. A group of beauties in bikinis were splashing around in the pool.

It made the old lechers want to go for a swim too.

Compared to their peers, Youke's event this year was planned far too conservatively.

Upon arriving at the main forum venue, the bigwigs of the gaming world were chatting and interacting.

As soon as Chen Guiliang appeared, several game company bosses and executives came over to congratulate him on the international award won by *The 7th Night*, a work from a company he had invested in.

Chen Guiliang also congratulated them on their games' hot sales. It was a mutual back-scratching affair.

Perfect World's CEO, Chi Yufeng, was surrounded by many people asking him about the considerations for a game company going public in the US. The situation was different every year, and asking Chi Yufeng for information was more appropriate than asking Chen Tianqiao or Ding Sanshi.

Tao Chenggang stood by Chi Yufeng's side the whole time. He was also entertaining the idea of taking Bailian Technology public.

Finally, the summit forum officially began.

The first keynote speaker was Director Kou from the GAPP, who emphasized that online games needed to bear cultural responsibility. He encouraged online games with cultural substance and resisted those with vulgar content. He also stressed that an anti-addiction system for online games must be launched this year. He then encouraged original, high-quality works, saying he would personally help original games to go overseas.

This was setting the tone for the industry.

The second speaker was Chen Tianqiao.

"We at Shanda resolutely support the GAPP. In the next two to three years, Shanda will shift its focus from primarily publishing foreign games to developing original domestic games..."

"To encourage original domestic games, Shanda has established the '18 Plan,' the '20 Plan,' and the 'Fengyun Plan,' raising 2 billion in cash to complete these three initiatives..."

The 18 Plan and 20 Plan were mentioned before.

The Fengyun Plan, however, was for acquiring game companies that had already achieved success. For example, the acquisition of Chengdu-based Jintian Technology cost Shanda over a hundred million. Its games included *Feng Yun Online* and *Legend Online*.

But although the company was acquired, the 23-year-old founder ran off with some of the development staff. They started a new company, created another impressive game, and sold it back to Shanda for over a hundred million yuan the following year.

It was awkward.

First, there was Dingguo Technology's *The 7th Night* winning an award, followed by Jintian Technology being sold for a high price of over a hundred million.

Chengdu was so stimulated by this that entrepreneurs flocked there. Within the next two or three years, hundreds of game development companies would emerge. The main creative personnel came primarily from Sichuan University and the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China.

Many students from Sichuan University and UESTC were developing games in their dorm rooms before they even graduated.

Thus, Chengdu gradually earned the nickname "City of a Thousand Games," and at its peak, there were indeed over a thousand game companies. Moreover, most of them were game development companies.

Besides Shanda, companies like Perfect World were also eyeing Chengdu. The major domestic game companies continuously sent people to Chengdu to acquire the development companies there.

Unlike later, when Chengdu was mentioned, the first thing that came to mind was gay culture.

After Chen Tianqiao's speech, Ding Sanshi took the stage.

Next was Charles Zhang.

Just as Charles Zhang walked onto the podium, the attendees weren't looking at him, but at The9's Jun Zhu.

In previous years at various game-related events, the first three speakers were invariably Chen Tianqiao, Ding Sanshi, and Jun Zhu.

How did Jun Zhu get pushed aside this year?

Could it be that because of the revision issues with the new *World of Warcraft* expansion, The9 had really fallen out with the GAPP?

Jun Zhu's face was a little grim.

Charles Zhang had already begun his speech, talking about everything from e-commerce to online communities, and then to portal websites and gaming communities. He claimed that Sohu would actively respond to the GAPP's call, focusing on self-developed domestic games and dedicating itself to spreading excellent Chinese culture.

As he talked, the topic shifted from *Tian Long Ba Bu* to the Olympics...

He was showing off as much as he could!

Ever since this fellow became the exclusive internet sponsor for the Olympics, no matter the occasion or topic of conversation, he would eventually steer it to the '08 Olympics.

"We are a portal matrix, and also the official website builder for the '08 Olympics. We have a team of several hundred people working on the Olympics, so our Olympic strategy is a massive strategy..."

"Everything related to the '08 Olympics and the internet will probably be related to us at Sohu. We will expand our entire technical team... And as for the position of games within this strategy, casual games are quite suitable for the Olympic strategy... We will be launching sports-themed casual games..."

The entire hall burst into enthusiastic applause.

There was no helping it; supporting the Olympics was the politically correct stance, and it was indeed something for the Chinese people to be excited about.

The real reason *World of Warcraft*'s new expansion was stuck in review was the upcoming Olympics, which led to stricter content censorship. Any content that could potentially be seen as an allusion had to be revised.

And The9's sensitivity was in the negative numbers. Was this something you could just bluff your way through? Even if you fooled Director Kou, who would Director Kou fool? The pressure was coming from above!

Sitting in the audience, Jun Zhu's face grew darker and darker as he listened to Charles Zhang's speech.

Ding Sanshi's expression was also complicated. NetEase was one of the big three in the anti-Sohu Olympic coverage alliance. Just a few days ago, he was giving instructions on how to attack Sohu, and today he was here applauding Charles Zhang's boasting.

Everyone thought that after Charles Zhang finished, it would surely be Jun Zhu's turn.

But the next speaker was Chi Yufeng.

Everyone thought: Jun Zhu is done for!

As someone who was always one of the first three speakers, he was still being kept off the stage this year. The GAPP wasn't giving Jun Zhu any face at all.

While Charles Zhang was there bragging about the Olympics, Chi Yufeng was, of course, bragging about taking games overseas.

He went on and on about traditional Chinese culture, saying that as long as the games were solid, expanding into overseas markets was also easy. *Perfect World* had already been sold in 16 countries and regions worldwide.

Then he talked about his experience of going public in the US, and how American investors were impressed by domestic games...

Director Kou listened with a beaming smile, especially fond of stories like this.

Finally, it was Jun Zhu's turn.

But what self-developed games did Jun Zhu have?

He first said that The9 would respond to the call to do self-development and to spread Chinese gaming culture. Then he immediately turned to talk at length about *Granado Espada*, saying that The9 had already secured the publishing rights for this game and was currently undergoing a technical handover with the Koreans.

He hyped *Granado Espada* to the skies, calling it a game that could rival *World of Warcraft*.

The smile on Director Kou's face vanished as he quietly listened to Jun Zhu brag about a Korean game.

Putting aside whether he was pandering to the leadership, the theme of today's summit forum was "Promoting Advanced Culture and Creating a Harmonious Internet."

Hadn't Jun Zhu's speech gone off-topic?

Even when Shi Yuzhu later took the stage, he spoke at length about *Zhengtu Online*'s "green" servers. He said *Zhengtu Online* aimed to build a harmonious online gaming community and create a green, domestic game.

Never mind whether Shi Yuzhu was bullshitting or not, at least he was willing to bullshit. Couldn't you, Jun Zhu, at least try to spin something?

Chen Guiliang still had a lot of clout now. After Jun Zhu came down, he went up right after, his speaking order even ahead of Lei Jun.

The publishers of *Audition Online* and *Crazyracing Kartrider* were all scheduled after Chen Guiliang.

This was because *Sanguosha* and *The 7th Night* had both brought honor to Director Kou overseas, and the theme of today's speech was promoting advanced culture.

"The name of our company, 'Game Science,' set the tone for self-development from the very beginning. We treat games as a science, we must be serious and responsible, and we must follow objective laws..."

"China has a rich wealth of historical and cultural themes worthy of being mined by game industry practitioners. If we don't dig, Japanese and Korean companies will. The Japs have already released a ton of games based on the Three Kingdoms and Journey to the West..."

"*Sanguosha* has not only been released in Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan, and Korea, but also in Singapore. And through our Singaporean publisher, it has been released throughout Southeast Asia. It is reported that *Sanguosha* is consistently ranked in the top five of online game charts in the Vietnamese market..."

"Next, we are considering selling it to the North American market, where there are a large number of Chinese players, as well as white and black players who appreciate Three Kingdoms culture..."

"Investing in Dingguo Technology was an inevitable accident. Since last autumn, we began to assemble a mobile game development team. Mobile games are also one of the future directions of gaming... Although *The 7th Night* is a horror game with a story set abroad, its game core discusses a common human theme, which is whether a person can face their own past..."

"In terms of single-player games, we have only made *Plants vs. Zombies* so far. Not only are the sales good, but the newly updated second chapter, priced at 2 yuan, has also seen many players make subsequent purchases..."

"*My Own Swordsman* is a big IP, and after acquiring the rights, we didn't dare to rush into development. The project leader first audited history classes at Tsinghua and Peking University and researched relevant materials from the Ming Dynasty. Currently, they are conducting field research on ancient architecture and traditional folk cultures across the country. We want to bring a real Ming Dynasty into the game..."

"When *My Own Swordsman* is sold overseas, we're going to give those foreign devils a little shock of Chinese history!"

Director Kou was happy again. Look at how well he spoke; games should indeed delve deep into traditional culture.

"*Future Era* will soon be officially open for registration. This game is a post-apocalyptic title. But it integrates Eastern and Western cultures and has a positive core. It doesn't use blood and violence to attract players, but rather the passionate spirit of humanity uniting as one, as well as a rich game story..."

At the end of the speech, Director Kou led the applause.

He would lead the applause for any speech he liked, and he had already done so several times.

The gaming tycoons listening to Chen Guiliang's speech, however, were focused on other things.

Game Science was continuously hiring and currently had close to 200 employees, but it was still considered a mid-sized company.

Such a mid-sized game company was already laying out plans for a game platform, single-player games, and mobile games, and it was rumored that they had also acquired an animation company.

Now they were about to launch a side-scrolling fighting game, as well as the highly anticipated *My Own Swordsman*, for which development had started at some unknown time.

Youke would be a formidable rival in the future!

Once *Future Era* becomes a hit, Youke would surely take off.

These big bosses were keeping a close eye on the official launch date of *Future Era*, deciding to coordinate and run promotions for their own games at the same time.

On the day *Future Era* goes live, it would find that all the major domestic companies' games were running promotions!

This included people who seemed to be on good terms with Chen Guiliang, like Shi Yuzhu and Chi Yufeng. They too would join the ranks to snipe at *Future Era*.
